subject: Phased onboarding plan & safety credits for annual prepay
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tara Olson <tara.olson@nimbushealth.com>, procurement <procure@procurecorp.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Phased onboarding plan & safety credits for annual prepay

Hi Tara —

Thanks again for the deep dive yesterday. Per our discussion, I'm proposing a phased approach for moving Nimbus from monthly/quarterly billing to a 12-month prepaid commitment that reduces unit cost but preserves a low-risk ramp for you. I attached a one-page credit schedule that shows how we would structure credits and true-ups during the first 6 months. High level: 

- Year 1 committed spend: $360k (annual prepay) with an optional 12-month ramp schedule.
- Initial cliff: first 30 days we hold to a conservative baseline (10% of monthly run-rate).
- Monthly true-up: usage above committed amounts rolls into next month; underutilization triggers safety credits per the attached schedule.
- Breakpoint concessions: if you cannot meet 60% of the committed usage by month 4, we step in with a one-time credit to offset the shortfall and transition to a quarterly true-up cadence.

Benefits to Nimbus: immediate unit price savings (~18% vs current monthly), simplified invoicing for finance, and a safety net while product usage ramps.

Can you share the procurement contact and any internal billing constraints (e.g., must be quarterly invoice, cannot prepay more than 12 months) so we can align legal and finance? If this looks directionally correct I'll convert the schedule to a formal term sheet.

Attachment: phased_onboarding_credit_schedule_v1.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

From: Tara Olson <tara.olson@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <procure@procurecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Phased onboarding plan & safety credits for annual prepay

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the note and the schedule. A few quick clarifying questions from procurement/finance:

1) Procurement prefers quarterly invoicing where possible — they say full prepaid contracts require an account receivable approval. Would Redwood accept a quarterly invoicing cadence while still applying the annual prepay discount (spread across four invoices)?
2) What are the mechanics of the safety credit? We need clear dates, formulas, and an example showing a 3-month underutilization scenario.
3) If Nimbus misses ramp milestones, what's the unwind process? Is there a penalty or simply credits?

We also want the term-sheet wording to allow a 30–60 day review by our legal team; they will likely push for a shortened auto-renew clause.

Looping procurement in for visibility — procure@procurecorp.com is now on thread.

Thanks,
Tara
Head of Product Operations | Nimbus Health
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 09:24:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Phased onboarding plan & safety credits — proposed concessions

Marissa / Laura —

Notes after sync with Finance: suggested compromise to keep the deal moving and satisfy procurement's quarterly invoicing ask. Draft concessions: 

- Discount: 20% off list pricing in Year 1 if Nimbus prepays the annual commitment but elects to be invoiced quarterly (we will invoice in 4 equal installments).
- Safety credits: If average monthly usage across months 1–4 is below 60% of expected run-rate, Redwood issues a one-time credit equal to 25% of the shortfall value (applied to remaining invoices).
- True-up cadence: monthly reporting to Nimbus, with the financial true-up performed quarterly (aligned to invoice dates).
- Unwind: if after month 6 actual cumulative usage < 40% of committed spend, either party may re-negotiate; a capped termination fee of 5% of remaining committed spend applies.

I attached the SOW draft and we can bake these points into the term sheet (Annual_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf will reflect these). Laura — confirm the 5% termination fee is workable from finance.

Attachment: SOW_draft_Nimbus_v2.docx

Thanks,
Ben
Account Director | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tara Olson <tara.olson@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: procurement <procure@procurecorp.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Phased onboarding plan & safety credits for annual prepay

Tara —

Per internal review, attached is a formal term sheet (v3) that implements the quarterly-invoice model while preserving the annual prepay economics. Key updates from the draft: 

- Commercial: 20% off list for Year 1 with 4x quarterly invoices (equal installments).
- Credits: Safety credit schedule (see section 3) — one-time credit equal to 25% of the shortfall if months 1–4 average <60% of target. Example included on page 2.
- True-up: usage tracked monthly; financial true-up only on quarter boundaries to match invoices.
- Early unwind: capped termination fee of 5% of the remaining commitment if cumulative usage <40% after month 6.
- Legal: 30-day review window and no auto-renew unless explicitly elected by Nimbus.

Please review the attached PDF and confirm procurement/legal contact for signature routing. When you're ready we'll open the DocuSign envelope (link below) and route to both billing and legal.

Attachment: Annual_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/rdw/nimbus-rdw-annual-prepay
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/54921/rdw-4521

Best,
Marissa
From: Tara Olson <tara.olson@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <procure@procurecorp.com>, legal@nimbushealth.com
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Phased onboarding plan & safety credits for annual prepay

Marissa —

Thanks — the term sheet looks clean and procurement is comfortable with the quarterly invoicing + the Year 1 discount. Legal wants one small change: contract language that allows a one-time reduction to Year 1 committed amount if we fail to launch a prioritized feature by month 3 that materially impacts usage (will propose wording). Otherwise we're good to proceed.

Next steps: I will route the term sheet internally (legal + billing) this week and expect to have a sign-off decision by Thurs. If approved, please send the DocuSign for signature and include the SOW draft for our implementation team.

Appreciate the flexibility — looking forward to getting this live.

—Tara
